title: What does the XRPL AuthorizedNFTokenMinter account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AuthorizedNFTokenMinter and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AuthorizedNFTokenMinter lets an issuer designate another account to mint NFTs on its behalf. [1]

NFTokenMinter identifies that authorized account. The documented removal procedure enables the option while omitting the minter field. This is a narrowly defined minting relationship, not transfer of the issuer's master key. Check both the account option and designated minter when deciding who may create tokens carrying that issuer identity. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for AuthorizedNFTokenMinter and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why AuthorizedNFTokenMinter is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
